hook.line: Everyone has the moment when it clicks: the café is losing money, or you have said the wrong thing. Spanish has one phrase for that moment, and it is not what English speakers expect.
hook.es: Me di cuenta de mi error demasiado tarde.
hook.en: I realised my mistake too late.

examples.es: Me di cuenta de mi error demasiado tarde.
examples.en: I realised my mistake too late.

examples.es: ¿No te das cuenta de que te está mintiendo?
examples.en: Don't you realise he's lying to you? (to a friend)

examples.es: Tomás se dio cuenta de que Rosa guardaba una carta.
examples.en: Tomás realised that Rosa was keeping a letter.

examples.es: Me di cuenta de que no tenía plata.
examples.en: I realised I had no money.

examples.es: No nos dimos cuenta de que era tarde.
examples.en: We didn't realise it was late.
Did you notice the price? (to a friend)

rule:
To realise or notice something, Spanish says *darse cuenta*: literally, to give yourself an account. It changes with who realises:

*me di cuenta*, I realised
*te diste cuenta*, you realised
*se dio cuenta*, he or she realised
*nos dimos cuenta*, we realised

Now: *me doy cuenta*, *te das cuenta*.

Then always keep the *de*: *de mi error*, *de que era tarde*, *del precio* (*de* + *el*). Don't use *realizar*: it means to carry something out.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a reflexive phrase: *dar* with a pronoun that points back at the person realising.

readAndPick.es: Me di cuenta de mi error demasiado tarde.
options: He realised my mistake too late.
I realised my mistake too late.
I made a mistake too late.

readAndPick.es: Tomás se dio cuenta de que Rosa guardaba una carta.
options: Rosa realised Tomás was keeping a letter.
Tomás wrote Rosa a letter.
Tomás realised that Rosa was keeping a letter.
Did I notice the price?
Did he notice the price?
Did you notice the price?

readAndPick.es: No nos dimos cuenta de que era tarde.
options: They didn't realise it was late.
We didn't realise it was late.
I didn't realise it was late.

readAndPick.es: ¿No te das cuenta de que te está mintiendo?
options: Don't you realise he's lying to you?
Doesn't he realise you're lying?
Didn't you realise he lied to you?

readAndPick.es: Me doy cuenta de que tienes razón.
options: I realised you were right.
You realise I'm right.
I realise you're right.

readAndPick.es: Me di cuenta de que no tenía plata.
options: I realise I have no money.
I gave him money.
I realised I had no money.

readAndPick.es: Mariana se dio cuenta del problema.
options: Mariana noticed the problem.
I noticed Mariana's problem.
Mariana didn't notice the problem.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *me di* or *se dio* and type the whole sentence: *Tomás ___ cuenta de que Rosa guardaba una carta.*
yourTurn.answer: Tomás se dio cuenta de que Rosa guardaba una carta.
yourTurn.why: Tomás is a he, so *se dio*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *cuenta de* or *cuenta* and type the whole sentence: *Me di ___ mi error demasiado tarde.*
yourTurn.answer: Me di cuenta de mi error demasiado tarde.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I realised I had no money.
yourTurn.answer: Me di cuenta de que no tenía plata.
yourTurn.why: *Me di cuenta de que* plus a whole clause.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Did you notice the price?
Type in Spanish: We didn't realise it was late.
yourTurn.answer: No nos dimos cuenta de que era tarde.
yourTurn.why: For we, *nos dimos*; *no* goes in front of the whole phrase.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about Mariana: *Me di cuenta del problema.* Say: Mariana noticed the problem.
yourTurn.answer: Mariana se dio cuenta del problema.
yourTurn.why: Mariana is a she, so *se dio*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a question to a friend: *Te das cuenta de que es tarde.* Say: Do you realise it's late?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Te das cuenta de que es tarde?
yourTurn.why: Same words with question marks; *te das* is for you.

pitfalls.right: Me di cuenta de mi error.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Realizar* means to carry something out. To realise is *darse cuenta de*.

pitfalls.wrong: Me di cuenta que era tarde.
pitfalls.right: Me di cuenta de que era tarde.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Keep the *de* before *que*, even though English has no word there.

pitfalls.wrong: Tomás dio cuenta de que Rosa guardaba una carta.
pitfalls.right: Tomás se dio cuenta de que Rosa guardaba una carta.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The little *se* is part of the phrase: you can't drop it.

personal: Think of something you realised this week. Say it with *Me di cuenta de que...*
